2. Answer Part 2: Spec DD (Specification-Driven Development)

Specification Contract Files: docs/lab-03/specification.md, docs/lab-03/api-spec.md, and docs/lab-03/ui-spec.md. All specifications were merged and approved in PR #37 prior to implementation PRs.

2.1 Numbered Functional Requirements (FR-01 to FR-20 Summary)
FR ID Module Requirement Summary
FR-01 to FR-06 Authentication & Session Email/password auth with bcrypt, HTTP-only signed cookie (toktickit_session), mandatory first-login password quarantine, /api/auth/me session check, and session termination via /api/auth/logout.
FR-07 to FR-10 Requester & Legacy Continuity Identity derived strictly from session (DevRequester retired), ticket creation and ticket viewing bound to authenticated requester, public comments, and Problem Appears Resolved indicator.
FR-11 to FR-15 IT Staff Operations Staff Ticket Queue with debounced text search, multi-filter dropdowns, sorting, and pagination. Claim ticket ownership, reassign staff, update IT Priority, and execute BR-15 permitted status transitions.
FR-16 to FR-20 Admin User Management User directory table with search and role filter, account creation with compliant initial password generator, edit account details, reset initial password, and enforce invariant safety guards (BR-16, BR-17).
2.2 Role-Based Authorization Matrix (RBAC)
Screen / Capability Requester IT Staff Administrator Enforcement Mechanism
Login / Logout / Change Password Allowed Allowed Allowed authenticateSession middleware
View Owned Tickets (/tickets) Allowed (Own) Allowed (Own) Allowed (Own) Filtered to req.user.id
Staff Ticket Queue (/staff/queue) Forbidden (403) Allowed Allowed requireRole(["IT_STAFF", "ADMINISTRATOR"])
Claim / Reassign Ticket Forbidden (403) Allowed Allowed requireRole(["IT_STAFF", "ADMINISTRATOR"])
Set IT Priority & Change Status Forbidden (403) Allowed Allowed BR-15 Permitted State Machine Validation
Public Comments Stream Allowed (Own) Allowed (All) Allowed (All) Shared ticket communication
Confidential Internal Notes Forbidden (403) Allowed Allowed Dual-channel confidentiality guard (BR-06)
User Management (/admin/users) Forbidden (403) Forbidden (403) Allowed requireRole(["ADMINISTRATOR"])
2.3 Database Migration Strategy & Product Definition of Done (DoD)

Migration Decisions: Adopted the Expand-and-Contract migration pattern. DevRequester records were preserved during transition and migrated directly into the unified User model with bcrypt hashes. Ticket.requesterId foreign keys were rebound to User.id without data loss. Legacy PENDING ticket status was preserved in schema while operational transitions strictly follow BR-14.

Product Definition of Done: (1) All 20 ACs pass in automated tests; (2) Zero DevRequester remnants in production client; (3) Clean Prisma migrations and idempotent seed; (4) 100% automated test suites passing; (5) Zero layout overflow on mobile (375px), tablet (768px), and desktop (1280px); (6) Documentation 100% written in English with zero em dashes.

AI Assistant Tooling: Google Antigravity Agent with Google Gemini. Full log in docs/lab-03/ai-use.md.

4.1 Selected Key Prompts Table
Prompt Topic Actual Prompt / Context Framing
Strategic Architecture & RBAC "Act as a Principal Software Architect. Analyze trade-offs between HTTP-only secure cookie sessions versus Bearer JWT. Define strict server-side RBAC invariants for Express + TypeScript + Prisma + React."
Formal Contract Synthesis (Spec DD) "Draft formal engineering specification for Sprint 3. Explicitly define: (1) Numbered Functional Requirements (FR-01+); (2) Invariant Business Rules (BR-01+) including admin safety guards; (3) Observable Acceptance Criteria (AC-01+)."
Defensive REST API Contract "Design complete REST API contract under /api. Ensure uniform JSON error responses. Ensure Requester attempts to access Internal Notes return 403 Forbidden."
DB Evolution & Seed (Issue #30) "Execute database evolution using Expand-Contract pattern: retain DevRequester during transition, migrate existing data to User with bcrypt hashes, update Ticket relations, and build idempotent seed script."
Auth Engine & Quarantine (Issue #31) "Construct authentication engine using signed cookies (toktickit_session). Build middleware detecting mustChangePassword: true and quarantining users to Change Password screen with live complexity checklist."
Comments Stream & Isolation (Issue #32) "Retire legacy /select-requester. Implement Public Comments stream and Problem Appears Resolved flag workflow without prematurely mutating ticket status to RESOLVED."
Staff Queue & Operations (Issue #33) "Build Staff Ticket Queue with multi-filter search, sorting, and pagination. Implement ticket claim/reassign, independent IT Priority, BR-15 permitted status transitions, and amber confidential internal notes."
Admin User Management (Issue #34) "Build User Management (/admin/users). Enforce safety invariants: mandatory initial password with safe generator, prevention of self-deactivation (BR-16), and prevention of deactivating the last active admin (BR-17)."
E2E Integration & QA (Issue #35) "Implement Playwright E2E suites covering E2E-01 to E2E-04. Capture responsive screenshot evidence across Desktop (1280x800), Tablet (768x1024), and Mobile (375x667)."
4.2 My Reflection on AI Use

Using an AI pair programmer with Spec-Driven Development (Spec DD) and Test-Driven Development (TDD) elevated velocity while enforcing architectural rigor. Dividing the AI into two roles: The Specification Agent for upfront RFC-style contract drafting and threat modeling, and The Coding Agent for test-backed implementation: prevented hallucination and scope creep. Human architectural oversight was vital in enforcing security invariants: ensuring server-side RBAC validation cannot be bypassed by client-side UI inspection, preserving administrative accounts against self-lockout, and executing zero-downtime database migrations without breaking legacy sprint test suites.

7.4 Direct API Authorization Evidence (Server-Side RBAC Verification)

The following real API execution traces prove that RBAC is enforced strictly at the Express middleware layer, rejecting unauthorized direct API calls even when requested with valid user session tokens:

# Test 1: Requester attempting to write confidential Internal Note (AC-10 / BR-06)
$ curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/staff/tickets/1/notes   -H "Cookie: toktickit_session=<VALID_REQUESTER_TOKEN>"   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"content": "Unauthorized attempt to create internal note"}'

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
{"error": "Access forbidden: Insufficient permissions"}

# Test 2: IT Staff attempting to access Administrator User Management (AC-20 / BR-05)
$ curl -i -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/admin/users   -H "Cookie: toktickit_session=<VALID_IT_STAFF_TOKEN>"

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
{"error": "Access forbidden: Insufficient permissions"}

# Test 3: Unauthenticated user attempting to query Staff Queue (BR-01)
$ curl -i -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/staff/tickets

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
{"error": "Authentication required"}
